title: Hosted API escalation: 5xx spikes, timeouts and noisy retries — incident response & permanent fixes
creator: Sara Kim
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported elevated 5xx responses and client-observed timeouts beginning 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Retry storms from SDKs amplified load and caused transient capacity exhaustion on several small host pools. This ticket tracks the escalation, triage, mitigations applied, root-cause analysis, and roadmap fixes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private where relevant.
impact_details: Affected: ~7% of requests across two small AZ host pools for the hosted API (us-east-1 region) over a 6 hour window. Symptoms: 502/503/504 and hanging connections; client SDKs retried aggressively (default exponential backoff misconfigured in older SDK pinned by customers). Customer escalations logged for 3 enterprise tenants (support tickets #RD-3142, #RD-3147, #RD-3150).
steps_to_reproduce: Send sustained 1000 rps request burst with varying prompt lengths to model endpoint r-inference-gpt-medium on small-pool nodes
Observe 20-40% request latency >5s, followed by 502/503 when worker processes OOM or hit internal request queue timeout
Run SDK clients with legacy retry config (max_attempts=6, backoff_base_ms=100) to see retry amplification causing queue backlog
updates: 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC — Pager duty: rotational on-call alerted after SLO alerts for hostpool us-east-1-small triggered. Initial mitigation: raised autoscale threshold and spun up extra small-pool instances (temporary capacity +30%). — Daniel Green
2026-03-09 23:05 UTC — Deployed temporary routing rule to divert traffic from most impacted pools to healthy medium-pool nodes; reduced immediate 5xx rate by ~70%. — Priya Shah

2026-03-10 02:30 UTC — Identified root signal: worker processes crashed due to a recent change in kv-cache eviction that increased peak memory usage for long-context requests (PR #github.com/redwood/serving@pr/2746). Reverted that change in canary and rolled back to stable kernel. — Miguel Alvarez
2026-03-10 04:00 UTC — Rolled wide rollback for affected runtime patch; latency and 5xx counts returned near baseline. Began tracking per-customer retry amplification metrics. — Miguel Alvarez

2026-03-11 09:30 UTC — Eng: submitted follow-up fixes: (1) add graceful rejection with informative 429 when queues are saturated, (2) increase internal request queue timeouts for multi-stage calls, (3) memory accounting for kv-cache to avoid unbounded growth. PRs: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2763, https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/2764. — Sara Kim

2026-03-12 15:00 UTC — Support: created customer-facing incident summaries for the 3 escalated tenants; offered credits and suggested SDK config updates. Support ticket links: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/RD-3142, RD-3147, RD-3150. — Alex Morgan

2026-03-13 11:45 UTC — Observability: added synthetic canary tests for long-context kv-cache scenarios and added a dashboard panel with per-pool OOM and queue_depth metrics. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/hosted/kv-cache-ooms. — Priya Shah
2026-03-14 08:00 UTC — Compliance: confirmed no data exfiltration and no PII exposure during the incident. Marked security_review_required = false. — Jordan Lee
analysis: Root cause: a regression in the kv-cache eviction algorithm increased per-request memory pressure for long-context workloads. This caused worker process OOMs and silent internal errors that returned 5xx responses. Secondary factor: several customers had pinned older SDK versions with aggressive retry defaults, which amplified load and prolonged the incident.
short_term_mitigations: Rolled back kv-cache eviction change on all affected pools (completed 2026-03-10)
Diverted traffic away from small pools to medium pools until capacity autoscaler tuned
Introduced temporary rate-limiting token bucket at edge for noisy tenants (support-approved) to cap retry amplification
Updated hosted API routing policy to prefer nodes with large memory headroom for long-context models
permanent_fixes: Implement memory-aware kv-cache with hard caps and backpressure signals rather than unbounded growth (target PR 2767)
Emit clearer client-facing 429/503 with structured error metadata and retry_after hint when internal queues are saturated
Ship runtime change that prefers graceful request rejection over process OOM; add circuit breaker to auto-fail expensive requests under pressure
Publish SDK guidance and release new SDKs with safer default retry/backoff config; tag legacy SDKs with advisory
Add automated synthetic tests in the CI that exercise kv-cache under long-context loads and assert memory budgets
resolution: Rollback of the kv-cache eviction regression restored baseline operation. Temporary routing and rate-limiting prevented immediate reoccurrence. Follow-up work (memory-aware cache, structured 429s, SDK release) scheduled and tracked in this ticket.
follow_up: ENG: complete memory-aware kv-cache implementation and land PR before next minor runtime release (owner: Miguel)
DX: prepare SDK v2.1 with conservative retry defaults and publish migration guide (owner: Developer Experience)
SRE: tune autoscaler policy thresholds and add proactive canaries for queue_depth > 60% (owner: Priya)
Support: run a customer outreach program to verify behavior for impacted tenants and close escalations (owner: Alex)
PM: update SLA page and incident communication template to include retry guidance for SDKs (owner: Lina Torres)
